_note: TEACHES THE ECONOMY. Won by owning a house AND fourteen villagers.
TWO WIN ROWS, AND THEY ARE ANDed. 'A house and fourteen villagers' is one objective in
two halves, which is exactly what multiple `win` rows mean (PLAN.md 11.8). An OR would
need grouping and no scenario wants one yet.
⚠️ FOURTEEN, AND THE NUMBER IS LOAD-BEARING: ONE HOUSE IS EXACTLY ENOUGH FOR IT.
The owner asked for 15 first, then corrected it to 14 on 2026-09-02: *"i did not account
for the scout in the pop cap, resuting in the player needing a second house."* THE SAVED
MAP GIVES EVERY PLAYER FIVE VILLAGERS AND ONE unit.scout_cavalry, so the opening
population is 6/10 and not 5/10. A town centre provides 10 and a house 5, so with one
house the cap is 15 -- which is 14 villagers PLUS THAT SCOUT, exactly. 15 villagers
would have been 16 population and a second house.
THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE TWO ROWS DEPEND ON EACH OTHER rather than merely sit beside each
other: the villager target is unreachable without the house the other row asks for, and
reachable with exactly the one it asks for. A target of 5 would be won on tick 0 (the
map already grants five) and would teach nothing; the lesson is that villagers make
villagers, and that villagers need housing.
HOW THE 15 WAS CAUGHT, because the method is the reusable part: it was play-tested to a
dead stop at 15/15 with fourteen villagers and a scout. The wrong arithmetic ('town
centre 10 + house 5 = 15, so one house exactly') had been written into this note, into
the briefing the player reads, AND into a passing test -- all three derived from
buildings.json and MapGen.STARTING_VILLAGERS, none of them from what the MAP grants.
dev_preview/PreviewScenarioWin.tscn prints the population as it drives each scenario to
its win, and its first line for this one reads `pop=6/10` for five villagers. See
PLAN.md 11.8: an authored target's reachability is a property of the map, not the roster.
test_campaigns now derives the house count from the map's own starting entities and
asserts it is EXACTLY ONE, so changing the target or removing the scout fails a test
rather than quietly making the briefing text a lie.
THE OPPONENT IS PASSIVE, which runs its whole economy and never attacks -- so this
scenario cannot be lost by being raided while you learn. Elimination is still the loss
(you own nothing, you are out), because that is true on every map in this game whatever
a file declares, which is why no lose condition is written here.
SCENARIO MODE MUST NOT LET CONQUEST WIN THIS, and as of 15.2 it does not: killing the
passive AI's five villagers and its town centre eliminates THEM and ends nothing, so
this cannot be won with two villagers and no house. WinConditionSystem._scenario is
where that fork lives -- conquest's loss without conquest's win.
A FOUNDATION IS NOT A HOUSE. ObjectiveSystem counts COMPLETE buildings only, which is
the population cap's rule and deliberately not the elimination rule's, so pegging out a
house and walking away does not tick this row.
name: How To Gather and Build
description: Villagers gather food, wood, gold and stone, and they build. Put up a house and grow to fourteen villagers.
message:
Objective: Build 1 house, and reach 14 Villagers.

Overview: Select a single villager and tap the build icon on the bottom left hand of the screen, tap the House tile, then drag the house to an open spot on the map where it turns GREEN and place it.

Select some villagers and tap on a berry bush -- look for an ORANGE tile flash to indicate they will gather it.

Train more villagers at your town centre. Your town centre houses 10 and the house adds 5, and you start with 5 villagers and a scout -- so that one house is exactly enough room for fourteen villagers.
_note_map: THE MAP IS THE SAVED map.png BESIDE THIS FILE (2.4c, PLAN.md 11.3). `seed` below is
PROVENANCE ONLY -- it records how the map was first generated and nothing reads it to
rebuild one. build_config() does not call MapGenerator at all, which is the owner's
ruling of 2026-09-01: generating is a one-off authoring step, not something a launch
does. That closed the 'a pinned seed is not a pinned map' defect for good, since
FastNoiseLite's float maths is not identical between an ARM phone and an x86 desktop.
